claim: Men's jeans average a 23.13 in front pocket height (maximum measured) against 14.33 in for women's, while back pockets are close: 16.01 in for men and 15.12 in for women.
The gender gap in average maximum front pocket height is 8.8 in.
In 29 of the 40 women's pairs the front pocket's maximum height is smaller than the back pocket's, while that happens in none of the 40 men's pairs.
Men's front pockets are on average 1.44 times as tall as their back pockets; women's are 0.95 times as tall, i.e. slightly shorter than their own back pockets.
Women's front pocket heights run from 11.5 to 21.5 in with a median of 14.0, while men's run from 20.0 to 28.0 with a median of 22.5.
Among women's jeans, boot-cut, skinny and straight styles average 14.25, 14.27 and 14.42 in maximum front pocket height, nearly identical across cuts.
Among women's jeans the average front pocket height ranges from 12.0 in at Guess and 12.35 in at Levi's to 17.5 in at American Eagle and 19.75 in at Abercrombie.
Price is unrelated to front pocket height: the correlation between price and maxHeightFront is -0.08.
Women's front pockets are also narrower: 15.18 in average maximum width and 12.26 in minimum width, against 16.37 in and 13.36 in for men.
The four shallowest front pockets are all women's pairs: Guess Power Stretch Skinny and J. Crew 8" Tooth Pick at 11.5 in, then Calvin Klein Midrise Skinny and Old Navy Original Boot Cut at 12.0 in.
The three deepest front pockets are men's: Wrangler Regular Fit at 28.0 in, Wrangler Slim Fit at 27.5 in and True Religion Geno Slim at 26.2 in.
Six men's pairs and three women's pairs are flagged with a pocket cutout in the data.
For 14 pairs the recorded maximum front height is smaller than the recorded minimum front height.
